Senator Lankford is right—America’s dependence on China for pharmaceuticals is a national security time bomb. The Medical Supply Chain Resiliency Act (H.R. 2213) proves Washington’s priorities are backward. Section 5(b)(2) requires partners to “maintain open trade during emergencies,” but why trust foreign regimes when we’ve seen China weaponize supply chains? The bill funnels $55 million into “regulatory cooperation” and “data flows” instead of rebuilding domestic production.

Meanwhile, the MAPS Act codifies Trump’s EO to audit supply chains, but both bills ignore the root problem: decades of outsourcing fueled by D.C.’s addiction to cheap foreign labor and lax regulations.

Real solutions require slashing FDA red tape, incentivizing U.S. pharma manufacturing, and treating medical sovereignty as non-negotiable. Until then, we’re funding our own vulnerability.
